# FastestJSONInTheWest - GitHub Copilot Instructions

> **SYNC POLICY**: This file MUST be kept in sync with `ai/CLAUDE.md`, `ai/copilot-instructions.md`, and `ai/gemini.md`. Last sync: October 2026.

## Project Context
High-performance C++23 JSON parser with **8x multi-register SIMD** acceleration (256 bytes/iteration), Turbo OnDemand lazy parsing (`fastjson::turbo::iterate`), Fused Tiled Tape DOM (`fastjson::turbo::dom_parser`), arena allocation, zero-copy `std::string_view`, 128-bit precision support, LINQ-style queries, and Mustache templating.

## Core Engines & Technical Architecture
- **Fused Tiled Tape DOM (`fastjson::turbo::dom_parser`)**:
  - Full document materialization on top of Turbo stage 1 (`s1_stream`, 64 KB L1-resident structural index window).
  - 16-byte `dom_node` tape with O(1) container skip (`next`), inline short strings (`<= 8` bytes stored directly in `payload` for single-word key comparisons), zero-copy `std::string_view` slices into the input buffer for unescaped strings `> 8` bytes, and a sparse backslash bitmap (`bs_bits`, 1 bit per 64-byte block) to invoke unescaping only when a block contains backslashes.
  - Zero-copy navigation types: `dom_element`, `dom_array`, `dom_object`, `dom_field`, `dom_type`.
  - Full integer fidelity up to 128 bits (`int64_t`, `uint64_t`, `__int128`, `unsigned __int128`) plus IEEE-754 binary64 `double`.
  - 1.04x–1.25x faster DOM parsing than simdjson DOM (2.51 ms vs 2.69 ms on AVX2; 4.82 ms vs 4.97 ms on AVX-512) and 1.23x–1.32x faster DOM field access (24.5 ns on AVX2, 48.8 ns on AVX-512).
- **Turbo OnDemand Engine (`fastjson::turbo::iterate`)**:
  - Lazy two-stage parsing with structural SIMD tape and deferred value materialization.
  - Software-pipelined 64-byte SIMD indexing (`build_indexes_avx2` / `build_indexes_avx512`), 64-byte space-padded SIMD tail buffer, and fast-advancing field search with inline numeric conversions.
  - 1.01x–1.21x faster than simdjson ondemand on AVX2 (Small: 52.8 ns vs 64.0 ns; Medium: 2.32 µs vs 2.35 µs; Large: 466.9 µs vs 470.2 µs).
- **Exact IEEE-754 Number Parsing (`to_double`, `to_double_general`, `scan_number_fast`)**:
  - Inline Clinger fast path (`mantissa < 2^53`, `|exp10| <= 22`) + `scan_number_fast` for `<= 15` digits.
  - 128-bit Eisel–Lemire algorithm (`modules/fastjson_pow5_128.h`, generated by `tools/gen_pow5_table.py`) with `std::from_chars` fallback for round-to-even boundaries.
  - Strict RFC 8259 grammar: rejects leading zeros, trailing decimals, `NaN`/`Infinity`, unclosed exponents, and truncating `get_int64` on floats; preserves `-0.0` sign bit.
- **Full RFC 8259 Stage-1 & Stage-2 Validation**:
  - SIMD UTF-8 validation (`validate_utf8` using Lemire/Keiser 3-nibble LUT in AVX2, with ASCII fast-path accumulator in stage 1).
  - Strict error reporting: `error_code::unescaped_control`, `error_code::unclosed_string`, `error_code::invalid_json`, `error_code::depth_exceeded`, and `error_code::trailing_content`.
- **Multi-Register SIMD**: 8x AVX2 ymm registers (256 bytes/iteration), 4x AVX-512 zmm, 4x SSE4.2/SSE2 xmm. GMF placement prevents Clang BMI serialization segfaults.

### Verified Benchmark Summary

**Local AVX2 Host (`--benchmark_repetitions=5` median, Clang 23.1.4):**
- Small (144 B, OnDemand): FastJSON **52.8 ns (2.73 GB/s)** vs simdjson 64.0 ns (2.25 GB/s) — **1.21x faster**
- Medium (13.2 KB, OnDemand): FastJSON **2.32 µs (5.69 GB/s)** vs simdjson 2.35 µs (5.60 GB/s) — **1.01x faster**
- Large (2.02 MB, OnDemand): FastJSON **466.9 µs (4.34 GB/s)** vs simdjson 470.2 µs (4.31 GB/s) — **1.01x faster**
- Small (144 B, DOM): FastJSON TurboDOM **203.1 ns (708.9 MB/s)** vs simdjson 253.7 ns (567.7 MB/s) — **1.25x faster**
- Medium (13.2 KB, DOM): FastJSON TurboDOM **5.58 µs (2.36 GB/s)** vs simdjson 5.83 µs (2.26 GB/s) — **1.04x faster**
- Large (2.02 MB, DOM): FastJSON TurboDOM **2.51 ms (807.2 MB/s)** vs simdjson 2.69 ms (753.1 MB/s) — **1.07x faster**
- Field Access (5 fields, DOM): FastJSON TurboDOM **24.5 ns** vs simdjson 32.4 ns — **1.32x faster**
- Array Iteration (DOM): FastJSON TurboDOM 134.4 µs vs simdjson **132.9 µs** — Tie (~1.1%)
- Array Iteration (OnDemand): FastJSON Turbo 866.9 µs vs simdjson **846.3 µs** — simdjson 1.02x faster

**AVX-512 Host (`oluwasanmiredhatserver`, `--benchmark_repetitions=5` median, Clang 23.1.1):**
- Small (144 B, OnDemand): FastJSON **96.2 ns (1.50 GB/s)** vs simdjson 104.0 ns (1.38 GB/s) — **1.08x faster**
- Medium (13.2 KB, OnDemand): FastJSON **3.87 µs (3.40 GB/s)** vs simdjson 4.34 µs (3.04 GB/s) — **1.12x faster**
- Large (2.02 MB, OnDemand): FastJSON 792.4 µs (2.56 GB/s) vs simdjson **743.8 µs (2.72 GB/s)** — simdjson 1.07x faster
- Small (144 B, DOM): FastJSON TurboDOM **412.3 ns (349.3 MB/s)** vs simdjson 481.1 ns (299.3 MB/s) — **1.17x faster**
- Large (2.02 MB, DOM): FastJSON TurboDOM **4.82 ms (420.1 MB/s)** vs simdjson 4.97 ms (407.5 MB/s) — **1.03x faster**
- Field Access (5 fields, DOM): FastJSON TurboDOM **48.8 ns** vs simdjson 60.1 ns — **1.23x faster**
- Array Iteration (DOM): FastJSON TurboDOM **183.3 µs** vs simdjson 260.3 µs — **1.42x faster**
- Array Iteration (OnDemand): FastJSON Turbo 1.62 ms vs simdjson **1.50 ms** — simdjson 1.08x faster
- Single Field Large (OnDemand): FastJSON Turbo 779.1 µs vs simdjson **757.8 µs** — simdjson 1.03x faster

## Testing & Quality Verification
- **`test_turbo_correctness`** runs **7,430 assertions across 26 sections**:
  - 180,000+ randomized & adversarial IEEE-754 number checks (`test_double_exact_known_cases`, `test_double_exact_randomized`)
  - 19,648,862 SIMD vs scalar differential UTF-8 buffer checks (`test_utf8_validator_differential`)
  - 3,000 randomized DOM round-trips + 16,000 mutation fuzz checks (`test_dom_randomized_roundtrip_and_mutation`)
  - Guard-page over-read protection (`test_guard_page_overread`): 1,211 documents flush against `mmap` + `mprotect` (`PROT_NONE`) guard page across `iterate()`, `parse()`, and `dom_parser::parse()` with zero 1-byte over-reads.
  - Dedicated regression test suites (`test_regressions_found_during_audit`): 5 suites covering `find_field` guard-page OOB, escaped-quote false matches, cross-key spans, `s1_stream::refill` unclosed string underflow, `bkt_stk` depth overflow, and `-0.0` / 8-digit boundary.
  - Multithreaded concurrency (`test_multithreaded_concurrent_parsing`): 8 threads × 40 iterations.
- **Rule 59 Sanitizers (`CMakeLists.txt`)**:
  - AddressSanitizer + LeakSanitizer + UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (`-DENABLE_ASAN=ON`): 3/3 `ctest` PASS (0 errors, 0 leaks).
  - MemorySanitizer with origin tracking (`-DENABLE_MSAN=ON`, using `cmake/msan_libcxx_compat.h` and `cmake/msan_libcxx_shim.cpp`): 3/3 `ctest` PASS (0 warnings).
  - ThreadSanitizer (`-DENABLE_TSAN=ON`): 3/3 `ctest` PASS (0 data races).

## Core API

### Parsing Modes
```cpp
// 1. Fused Tiled Tape DOM (materialized tree, zero-copy nodes)
fastjson::turbo::dom_parser dom_p;
auto doc = dom_p.parse(json_string);
if (doc) {
    fastjson::turbo::dom_element root = *doc;
    auto val = root["key"];
    if (val && val->is_string()) {
        std::string_view s = *val->get_string();
    }
}

// 2. Turbo OnDemand (lazy, fast-advancing search)
fastjson::turbo::turbo_parser tp;
auto ondemand_doc = fastjson::turbo::iterate(json_string, tp);

// 3. Eager AST DOM / Arena
auto eager_doc = fastjson::parse(json_string);
auto arena_doc = fastjson::parse_arena(std::move(json_string));
```

### Key Types
- `fastjson::turbo::dom_parser` — owns tiled buffers and tape for DOM parsing
- `fastjson::turbo::dom_element` — zero-copy DOM node view
- `fastjson::turbo::dom_array` — zero-copy DOM array with iterator and `at()`
- `fastjson::turbo::dom_object` — zero-copy DOM object with `find_field()` and `operator[]`
- `fastjson::turbo::dom_field` — key-value pair holding `std::string_view` key and `dom_element` value
- `fastjson::turbo::dom_type` — node type enumeration
- `json_value` — AST node (eager parse result)
- `json_document` — owns input + arena + root value (arena parse)
- `ondemand_document` — owns input + structural tape (lazy parse)

## Architecture Notes
- SIMD implementations live in `namespace fastjson::detail` inside the Global Module Fragment
- Thin inline wrappers in the module purview delegate to `detail::` functions
- The structural tape (`modules/fastjson_simd_index.h`) indexes structural characters ({, }, [, ], ,, :, ") plus primitive starts (t, f, n, digits)
- The AVX2 scanner tracks `in_string` state within 32-byte chunks to avoid false structural indexing
